ai.title: Commander agent added
ai.summary: New `.agents/commander.ts` defines a `commander` agent using `x-ai/grok-4-fast` to execute terminal commands via `run_terminal_command`. The agent yields the command execution step then passes output to the model for concise analysis based on specific extraction prompts. Scope is limited to the internal agent definitions directory.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command, it now uses a faster model called grok-4-fast to execute and analyze the output before relaying a concise summary back to you. Previously the assistant would run commands but the analysis step was less streamlined. This means you get quicker, more focused responses when the assistant needs to inspect system information, run diagnostics, or check logs, without waiting for slower processing. The feature is live today in the internal agent definitions.

ai.title: Overhaul base2 agent with editing tools and commander subagent
ai.summary: Updated `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to grant `base2` direct file editing capabilities by adding `str_replace` and `write_file` to `toolNames`. The `read-only-commander` spawnable agent was replaced by the full `commander` agent. Prompt logic was refined to allow `base2` to handle trivial edits directly, reducing reliance on spawning editor subagents for minor changes.

eli5.text: The main assistant can now make small text edits to files directly instead of always handing the job to a separate editor agent, so quick fixes happen faster. It also gained access to the full commander agent instead of only a read-only version, giving it more flexibility when it needs to coordinate work. If you use this assistant, simple changes look less like a multi-step handoff and more like a single, direct action.

ai.title: Add independent-thinker agent
ai.summary: New `.agents/independent-thinker.ts` defines a stateless analysis agent using `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`. It ignores message history and parent system prompts to prevent context pollution, accepting `filePaths` for direct reading. Registered in `base2.ts` to handle key self-contained decisions, while `decomposing-thinker` retains planning and context-gap checks.

eli5.text: When the assistant decides how to plan a coding task, it now occasionally brings in a fresh second opinion before settling on a plan. This new reviewer isn't told about the earlier back-and-forth with you, so it examines your request purely on its own merits rather than being influenced by previous discussion. The net effect is that some key decisions get a clean-slate review, which should reduce cases where the plan quietly drifts from what you actually asked for. This behavior is already in effect for tasks that run through the main planning flow.

ai.title: BuffBench2 eval harness added
ai.summary: New BuffBench2 evaluation suite introduced via `evals/buffbench/` directory. `agent-runner.ts` executes agents on commits using `CodebuffClient` with 10-minute timeouts, capturing diffs, context files, costs, and step traces. JSON eval datasets (`eval-codebuff.json`, etc.) define specific tasks with SHAs and prompts for repo-based testing. `judge.ts` and `main.ts` orchestrate scoring and execution, expanding internal benchmarking capabilities.

eli5.text: A new automated testing system for AI coding agents has been added to the codebase. This system can now run AI agents against specific programming tasks, automatically track their work including time and costs, and score their performance. If you look at the repository, you'd see a brand new folder dedicated to these evaluation tools that weren't there before, making it possible to compare how different AI assistants handle real coding challenges.

ai.title: buffbench analyzer tweaks
ai.summary: Updated buffbench analyzer to use commit.prompt instead of commit.spec for task output formatting. Adjusted trace-analyzer recommendations schema to exclude code improvement suggestions.

eli5.text: When the system analyzes how a helper assistant performs on tricky tasks, it now prints the assistant's actual instructions in its write-up instead of a technical task label. Also, it tells the assistant doing the analysis not to suggest ways to rewrite the code itself, only to comment on how the helper assistant and its process could work better. These are internal tools used to review assistant performance, so nobody outside the team sees a difference day to day.

ai.title: Extend buffbench agent timeout to 30 minutes
ai.summary: Increased agent execution timeout in evals/buffbench/agent-runner.ts from 10 to 30 minutes. Adjusts the `timeoutMs` constant passed to `withTimeout` to accommodate longer-running tasks. Affects only the buffbench evaluation runner.

eli5.text: The system that tests AI assistants on tricky coding tasks now lets those assistants run for up to 30 minutes instead of stopping them at 10 minutes. If you run or watch these internal evaluations, some previously-failing tests may now complete successfully because they have more time to finish. This adjustment only affects the internal testing tool, not any product you use.

ai.title: Exclude commits with agent errors from BuffBench scores
ai.summary: run-buffbench.ts now tracks commit SHAs with agent errors via `commitShasWithErrors` and excludes all runs from those commits when calculating average score, cost, and duration. Previously, only individual failed runs were filtered, potentially skewing metrics if one agent errored on a commit while others succeeded. The change ensures consistent comparison across agents by removing entire problematic commits from the evaluation set. Console output now notes the number of excluded commits.

eli5.text: When the system scores how well different AI assistants perform on coding tasks, it now throws out entire batches where any assistant hit an error, instead of just skipping the individual failed attempts. You would notice this in the reported results, which now exclude any task group that had problems, keeping the comparison fair across assistants. The system also prints how many of these error-prone groups it left out.

ai.title: Refactor buffbench output formatting
ai.summary: Extracted task result formatting into new `formatTaskResults` function in `evals/buffbench/format-output.ts`. `run-buffbench.ts` now imports this single function instead of manually orchestrating `formatAgentResult` and `formatTraceAnalysis` with raw `console.log` calls. Scope limited to eval harness internals; no user-facing CLI or Web changes.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation system that measures how well different AI assistants perform has been reorganized so that all of the result-printing logic now lives in one place instead of being spread across multiple spots in the main runner file. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping, nothing visible to you changes when running the benchmark, and no outputs, formats, or behaviors are altered. It just makes the code easier to maintain for the engineers who build on top of this evaluation tooling.

ai.title: base2 workflow prefers single editor over parallel spawns
ai.summary: Updated `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to recommend spawning a single editor for implementation steps instead of two. Added explicit guidance to avoid multiple parallel editors unless handling large independent changes. This reduces cost and improves result consistency for standard tasks.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal helper now does its work in one go instead of splitting the same job across two helpers at once. This affects other developers building on top of the base2 agent: their implementation steps will run through a single editor rather than the previous pair, and the documentation now explicitly says to keep parallel editors to large, independent jobs only. If you looked, the change log would show you the step that used two editors collapsed into one, plus a new guideline telling authors not to spawn multiple editors unless they are handling big, unrelated changes.

ai.title: Refine agent prompts for conciseness and remove file-q-and-a
ai.summary: Updated system and instruction prompts in `base2`, `code-sketcher`, and `file-picker` to enforce stricter output conciseness, removing final summaries and redundant formatting. `base2` now explicitly suppresses final summaries. `code-sketcher` instructions tightened to prevent sketching obvious code or duplicating helpers. `file-picker` switched to `FILE_TREE_PROMPT_SMALL` and removed `stepPrompt`. `find-all-referencer` dropped `file-q-and-a` from spawnable agents.

eli5.text: The AI assistants that help edit code have been told to be more concise and stop writing summaries at the end. When you ask one of these assistants to change code, it will now give you shorter explanations and skip the recap at the end. The file-finding helper also got simpler instructions, and one of the assistants can no longer call upon a reference-checking tool to look up facts about specific files.

ai.title: find-all-referencer model update
ai.summary: find-all-referencer model switched from x-ai/grok-4-fast to x-ai/grok-code-fast-1 for speed. base2.ts prompt updates reflect this change and remove redundant change descriptions. Internal agent routing and prompt logic only. No user-facing features or breaking changes.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes helper that the internal development tools use to search through code has quietly switched to a faster version of its underlying engine. This means the internal agent that finds where things are defined or referenced across the codebase now runs a bit quicker when developers trigger it through the base2 agent's suggested actions. Nothing about the commands you give or the results you get has changed; the swap just makes that particular search step snappier for anyone working inside the development environment today.

ai.title: base2 prompt tweaks
ai.summary: Updated `.agents/base2/base2.ts` prompt guidelines. Clarified reviewer spawning rules for trivial vs. most changes. Added explicit instruction to avoid creating unrequested summary markdown files.

eli5.text: You're an agent following a set of operating instructions. The guidance got two small clarifications: it now spells out that you should skip spawning a separate reviewer for tiny follow-up tweaks, and it explicitly tells you not to generate a summary markdown file the user didn't ask for. If you run this assistant today, it will be slightly more selective about when it asks for a review and won't leave behind an extra summary document.

ai.title: Add 10-minute timeouts to buffbench judge and trace analyzer
ai.summary: Wraps `client.run` calls in `withTimeout` (10m limit) within `evals/buffbench/judge.ts` and `evals/buffbench/trace-analyzer.ts`. Prevents indefinite hangs during eval execution. Minor cleanup in `run-buffbench.ts` removes verbose prompt logging.

eli5.text: The automated system that runs and reviews coding tests will now give up after 10 minutes instead of waiting forever. If one of the two review steps (the judge that scores results or the analyzer that summarizes traces) ever gets stuck, it will stop and move on rather than hanging the whole process. A small bit of extra logging was also removed so the run output stays cleaner.

ai.title: Buffbench trace analysis uses prompt, handles errors, runs
ai.summary: Trace analysis in evals/buffbench/run-buffbench.ts and evals/buffbench/trace-analyzer.ts now uses commit.prompt instead of commit.spec. The analyzeAgentTraces function signature updated to accept codingAgentPrompt. Error handling wrapped in try/catch using getErrorObject. Analysis executes regardless of agent count, removing previous commitTraces.length > 1 guard.

eli5.text: The automated grading system now examines each completed task by looking at the exact instructions that were given, instead of a rough summary of them, and it keeps running to finish its analysis instead of stopping early when there is only one task. If the analysis hits a problem, it now catches the error and continues rather than crashing. You would notice this by seeing complete reports for every run, even ones with a single agent, instead of missing or incomplete ones.

ai.title: buffbench: refactor runTask, delete onProgress
ai.summary: Extracted runTask into a standalone async function in `evals/buffbench/run-buffbench.ts` to modularize agent execution and trace handling. Removed `onProgress` callback support from `evals/buffbench/main.ts` and deleted the `ProgressEvent` type from `evals/buffbench/types.ts`. This simplifies the evaluation runner interface by handling progress logging internally within the task loop rather than via external callbacks.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team cleaned up how the system runs and watches its automated coding tests. Previously, an external piece of code could be notified whenever a test passed, failed, or started, and this notification used a now-deleted set of message types. That callback and those message types were removed; now the test runner handles all status updates internally instead of reporting them out. The visible result to anyone watching is only a small change in how those status messages are produced internally; no external behavior or output changes for users.

ai.title: Fix missing instructions prompt when no user prompt provided
ai.summary: Removed conditional check preventing instructions prompt generation when user prompt was empty. Instructions are now always fetched via getAgentPrompt regardless of prompt presence, while user message inclusion remains conditional. This fixes bug in backend/src/run-agent-step.ts where agent templates with instructions but no initial prompt failed to apply system instructions.

eli5.text: If you run an AI helper that has built-in instructions but no starting message of its own, those instructions will now be applied instead of being skipped. The system previously waited for a user message before loading the helper's instruction page, so helpers with instructions but no initial prompt ran without any guidance. It is live today for any of those instruction-only helpers.
